doc.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Growing up with Basie records; Freddie Green
summary: Gitler's older brother's Basie fandom, the 1938 Manhattan Center dance, Old and New Testament bands, and Freddie Green turning up in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: and probably his favorite band was the Basie band. So that was what I cut my teeth on, among other bands. And I remember him telling me, “Listen to the way Lester Young starts the band off on ‘Every Tub.’” Because he had the first lick before the band even came in. And my brother was twelve years older than I was and you know, he was like a second father in a way. He used to take me out with his friends and, you know, I looked up to him and I found that this interest he had touched me. I didn’t have to think twice about it. It got me in my soul. And he belonged to a young folks league which did charity raising for an orphanage. And every Sunday afternoon they’d have a dance over at the orphanage and they’d play all these records and dance to them. Well Christmas 1938 they hired the Basie band to play at the Manhattan Center in New York as their big fundraiser. And I remember waiting for him to get up that next morning so he could tell me about actually seeing all these people that I’d been listening to on record. So the Basie band is very special to me. And I cherish those early records. And you know they always say that’s the Old Testament band, and then the band that he formed after he had the sextet for a brief time in 1950, when he started up the band again in ‘51, that’s called the New Testament band. And they had, in common, the incredible swing, and Freddie Green that made the transition. They tell the story that when Basie formed the sextet, he was opening at the Capitol Lounge I think in Chicago and he hadn’t notified Freddie Green, he hadn’t hired him. And Freddie Green just came there, plugged in his amplifier and he was there. So naturally Basie had to hire him.
What are you going to do, tell him to go home?

No way. And he was like the core of that rhythm section, which they call the All- American Rhythm Section, and it was. So he was the constant. He went from the original band to the sextet, octet, whatever it happened to be at the time, and then the new band, which of course is where Joe Williams comes in.
